extracted.intended_audience: applicants for plant variety certificates, plant breeders, intellectual property practitioners, and national IP offices
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for filing, examination, denomination, issuance, maintenance, enforcement, and remedies relating to plant variety certificates. Covers documentary requirements, technical examination (DUS), publication, oppositions/ownership claims, rights conferred, exceptions, fees, duration, and administrative and judicial remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must attach to his application, or submit within six months, (a) a written statement specifying the date and number of the earlier filing, the country and the name of the applicant; and (b) a certified copy of the earlier application. Where there are two or more earlier applications, priority may be based only on the earliest application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit these items in due time results in loss of the benefit of the priority right; any item received more than six months after filing shall be declared inadmissible. Priority has the effect of deeming the application filed on the first application's filing date for protection conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of priority and deferment of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority causes the application to be deemed filed on the filing date of the first application with regard to protection conditions. The applicant may request deferment of examination for not more than two years from expiry of the priority term or three years from the filing date of the first application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the first application is rejected or withdrawn, examination may commence earlier; in that case the applicant shall be afforded a reasonable period to furnish required information/documents/materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissibility due to non-payment
rubrics_metrics.description: No application shall be admissible if it is not accompanied by a document proving payment of the prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of payment is a strict precondition to admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date allocation and minimum contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall allocate as the filing date the date of receipt provided that at receipt the application contains: (i) information establishing the identity of the applicant; (ii) the description of the variety; and (iii) proof of payment of filing and publication fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If items of Article 13(2) are missing, the Organization will request corrections and will allocate as filing date the date of receipt of corrections; failure to correct within time results in the application being deemed not filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of other defects
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application contains defects other than the mandatory items for filing date, the Organization shall invite the applicant to rectify; failure to rectify within the time allowed means the application is deemed not to have been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Organization issues invitations to rectify non-filing-date defects and sets time limits for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish a notice of filing of the application containing the items mentioned in Article 13(2)(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication triggers opposition and ownership-claim time limits and starts certain provisional protections/exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to file objections after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Once published, any person may file written and reasoned objections within three months; a fee is charged on filing an objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections may be filed exclusively to assert that the variety is not new, distinct, uniform or stable or that the applicant is not entitled to protection. Applicant may respond within three months (renewable once); parties may be heard; Organization's ruling is appealable to the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days of notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership before the Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: When a person entitled to the certificate believes a non-entitled person filed the application, the entitled person may claim ownership before the Organization within three months from publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Organization sends the claim to the applicant who may reply within a once-renewable three-month period; parties may be heard before decision; decision is appealable to the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days; Organization shall transfer the application to the claimant if the claim is valid and publish final decisions in the special register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and substance examination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine the application as to form and substance to verify: (a) allocation of a filing date per Article 16; (b) documents are complete and satisfy Articles 13 and 14; (c) the application is not excluded under Article 3; (d) the variety applied for is new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incomplete or non-conforming, the Organization invites put-in-order within three months (extendable 30 days for justifiable need); corrected applications retain the initial filing date; failure to put in order = deemed not filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical (DUS) examination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A technical examination based on growing trials and other necessary tests shall be carried out to ensure: (a) the variety belongs to the specified taxon; (b) the variety is distinct, uniform and stable (DUS); and (c) where conditions are satisfied, to establish the official description of the variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical examination shall be conducted by an authorized institution approved by the Organization; the Organization may rely on results from Contracting Party services; the Organization determines practical conditions for the examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of information, documents and plant material for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is required to provide all information, documents or material required by the Organization for technical examination; failure entails rejection unless good grounds exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The creator may be required to submit additional information and the plant material required for technical examination. The cost of technical examination is borne by the applicant and payable directly to the Organization; the Organization establishes a schedule of fees by principal botanical taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall be kept secret by the Organization and services/institutions involved; access to information concerning applications shall be regulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No information relating to applications may be disclosed without breeder consent, except in special cases determined by the Organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rejection of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be rejected prior to registration if: (a) the applicant is not entitled; (b) applicant has not responded within prescribed time to rectification notices (erroneous/incomplete info or material irregularity); (c) the variety does not satisfy requirements of Articles 4–8 or belongs to an excluded botanical taxon under Article 3; (d) applicant refuses or is unable to propose an acceptable denomination per Articles 26–30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Organization shall notify, record and publish rejection; rejection is appealable before the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days; Organization may correct obvious clerical errors despite paragraph (1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the plant variety certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing a certificate, the plant variety certificate shall bear: (a) number of the certificate; (b) number of the filing; (c) filing date; (d) identity of botanical taxon; (e) denomination of the variety; (f) corporate name or name and surname of owner and address; (g) validly claimed priority, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The official technical description shall be attached to the plant variety certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of the certificate and description
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish, for each plant variety certificate, the information in Article 24 and the name and address of the agent, and shall publish the official technical description of the variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing regulations define publication arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denomination as generic designation and admissible signs
rubrics_metrics.description: The denomination shall constitute the generic designation of the variety and may consist of any word, combination of words, figures, letters and figures, with or without meaning, provided they serve to identify the variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a denomination already used or registered in a Member State or Contracting Party exists, only that denomination may be used before the Organization unless grounds for refusal exist; synonyms shall be recorded in registers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on confusingly similar designations
rubrics_metrics.description: For as long as the variety is exploited, it is prohibited in Member States to use a designation identical or confusingly similar to the denomination of that variety in relation to another variety of the same or closely related species; prohibition remains after exploitation where denomination has acquired particular significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition also applies to denominations registered in Contracting Parties. Persons marketing propagating material of a protected variety must use the denomination; obligation continues beyond the certificate term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted concurrent use of trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permissible to use a trademark, service mark, trade name or similar designation in conjunction with the registered variety denomination, provided the denomination remains easily recognizable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior rights of third parties shall not be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for refusal of a denomination
rubrics_metrics.description: A designation shall be refused registration as a denomination if it: (a) does not conform to Article 26; (b) is not suitable for identifying the variety (distinctiveness or linguistic suitability); (c) is contrary to public policy or morality; (d) consists exclusively of signs/indications that denote species, quality, quantity, intended purpose, value, geographical origin or time of production; (e) is liable to mislead/confuse as to characteristics, value, origin or links; (f) is identical/confusingly similar to a denomination of an existing variety of same or closely related species in Member States or Contracting Parties (with limited exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration shall also be refused for a designation including an element that hampers free use (e.g., trademark elements that would be refused under trademark law); such designations can be refused on opposition by the owner of rights in the element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denomination registration procedure and deferral
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed denomination shall be filed at the same time as the application. On payment of a special fee and proposal of a provisional designation, the applicant may defer the denomination registration procedure; the applicant must submit the proposed denomination within the time limit specified or the application will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Organization shall publish the denomination proposal unless it notes grounds for refusal; the proposal is communicated to relevant services in Contracting Parties. The denomination is registered at the same time as the plant variety certificate is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to denomination registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any concerned person may, within the prescribed time limit, file opposition to registration of a denomination based on grounds in Article 27. Relevant services of Contracting Parties may submit observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions and observations are communicated to the applicant for response or a new proposal; non-conforming proposals trigger requests to submit new denominations and can lead to rejection; Organization decisions on opposition are appealable to the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture and replacement of denomination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall declare a registered denomination forfeit if: (a) it was registered despite existence of grounds for rejection; (b) the owner requests forfeiture invoking legitimate interest; or (c) a third party produces a court decision prohibiting use of that denomination in connection with the variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner is advised and invited to propose a new denomination within the time limit; the Organization may make the proposal if variety no longer protected. New proposal is subject to examination and publication; new denomination registered and published once approved and former denomination cancelled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive rights conferred by certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Under conditions and within limits laid down, the plant variety certificate confers on its owner the exclusive right to exploit the variety and to prohibit any person from exploiting it; the owner can assign or transfer the certificate and conclude license contracts; owner may institute legal proceedings against infringers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner also has rights to act against misuse of denomination or failure to use denomination where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'exploitation'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of rights, 'exploitation' means acts carried out in relation to propagating material: (a) production/reproduction; (b) processing for propagation; (c) offering for sale; (d) sale/marketing; (e) export; (f) import; (g) stocking for those purposes. It also covers similar acts in relation to harvested material and products made directly from harvested material obtained through unauthorized use, and varieties essentially derived or not clearly distinguishable or requiring repeated use of protected variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope subject to Articles 33 and 34 exceptions and extensions to essentially derived varieties and varieties not clearly distinguishable or requiring repeated use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from rights (permitted acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights do not extend to: (a) private non-commercial acts; (b) experimental or research acts; (c) acts for purpose of breeding other varieties (except where Article 32(4) applies); (d) use by a farmer on his own holding for propagation of harvested material obtained by cultivating a protected variety (not applying to fruit, forestry or ornamental plants); (e) acts by third parties in good faith prior to filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exemptions delimit enforcement and are subject to specified exclusions (e.g., fruit/forestry/ornamentals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights do not extend to acts concerning material of the protected variety that has been sold or otherwise marketed on the territory of a Member State by the owner or with his consent, or material derived from such material, except where acts involve further propagation or export to a country that does not protect varieties (unless intended for consumption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhaustion prevents owner from controlling downstream acts except where propagation or certain exports are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from market control measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights conferred by a plant variety certificate are independent of measures adopted by Member States controlling production, certification and marketing of variety material or import/export.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National market-control regimes do not alter the substantive rights conferred by the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of certificate and maintenance by fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraph (2), a plant variety certificate shall expire 25 years after its date of issue. To maintain the certificate, an annual fee shall be paid in advance each year, first due one year after issue. A six-month grace period is allowed with an additional fee; failure to pay results in forfeiture of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance requires timely annual fees; grace period and additional fee conditions are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection from filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant shall enjoy all the rights provided from filing of the application, provided that proceedings for damages occasioned through the defendant's fault after publication of the application may not be instituted until the plant variety certificate has been issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing confers provisional protection but limits on damages claims apply until issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of protection after non-renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: If protection has not been renewed for reasons beyond the owner's control, the owner may request restoration within six months of cessation of reasons and not later than two years from the date renewal was due, on payment of required annual and restoration fees, and filing documentary evidence and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization examines reasons and may restore or reject; restoration does not prolong the original term; restoration decisions are appealable to the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government exploitation (compulsory/licensed use) and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The government may decide that a variety shall be exploited without owner's consent by a State service or designated third party when public interest (food supplies/public health) demands or to remedy anti-competitive exploitation, subject to payment of equitable remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: owner must have been put on formal notice to remedy and failed; designated party must be competent; three years must have elapsed since issue. Government specifies authorized acts, duration and remuneration; may require owner to supply propagating material on payment; authorizations are non-transferable except with the enterprise and do not exclude owner's exploitation or license contracts; exploitation serves domestic market only; parties heard and decisions are appealable to competent administrative court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner's obligation to maintain the variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner is required to maintain the protected variety or its hereditary components, at his own expense, throughout the certificate's validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the Organization's request, owner must furnish information/documents/materials within prescribed time to any authority designated for verifying maintenance; failure may lead to forfeiture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples and official sample maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner is required to furnish, at his own expense and within the time allowed, suitable samples of the protected variety (or hereditary components) to any authority designated by the Director-General for establishing/renewing the official sample or for comparative examination for protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The owner may be required to maintain or preserve the official sample himself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of ownership, assignments and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to a plant variety certificate and the certificate itself may be assigned or transferred by succession. Any change of ownership must be recorded in writing, registered by the Organization and is not binding on third parties unless recorded in the special register; the Organization shall publish a notice of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licenses (exclusive/non-exclusive) must be evidenced in writing and recorded in the special register and are not binding on third parties until registered and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall deprive the owner of the certificate if it is established that he has failed in maintenance obligations and the variety is no longer uniform or stable, or if owner fails to respond to verification requests or if denomination forfeited and owner does not propose a suitable new denomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forfeiture may not be declared until owner is put on formal notice to meet obligations within a reasonable notified period; forfeiture takes effect on date of its registration and is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of procedural time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Organization deems justified, it may, on written request and on specified conditions, extend prescribed time limits for performing acts or taking steps under this Annex or implementing regulations, even if the time limit has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are discretionary and subject to conditions specified by the Organization; decision notified to concerned parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent courts and summary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil actions relating to plant varieties shall be brought before competent domestic courts and judged as summary proceedings. Domestic criminal courts hearing infringement shall rule on defenses, invalidation/forfeiture and ownership issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National courts handle civil/criminal matters; procedural form is summary in civil cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of the certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person with legitimate interest may file a request for invalidation. The court shall invalidate the certificate if it is established that (a) the variety was not new or distinct on the filing or priority date; or (b) where issuance was essentially based on applicant-submitted info/documents, the variety was not uniform or stable on that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invalidated certificate is deemed invalid as of its date of issue; the decision is notified to the Organization which shall register and publish it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership before the court (post-issuance)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the certificate has been issued, claims of ownership must be filed before the competent domestic court; action lapses within three years from issuance of the registration certificate, except actions against defendants acting in bad faith which are not time-barred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court decisions on transfer are notified to the Organization, registered and published; licensees entered in the special register are notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of infringement and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Articles 33, 34 and 39, acts referred to in Article 31 carried out on the territory of a Member State by a person other than the owner without consent constitute infringement. Acts prior to publication of issuance are not considered infringements; acts subsequent to notification of the certified true copy may be prosecuted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may grant injunctions to cease or prevent infringement, award damages and other remedies under domestic laws. Licensees may initiate proceedings and owners may participate; licensees may intervene to obtain compensation. Courts may award remedies similar to unfair competition actions at request of competent authorities or associations (e.g., breeders, seed producers, farmers).
